summary.text: A 13-year-old female with severe, infantile-onset atopic dermatitis had inadequately responded to azathioprine, cyclosporine, methotrexate, mycophenalate mofetil, phototherapy and omalizumab. Before biologic treatment her EASI was 40.1 and cDLQI 15. She was started on dupilumab 200 mg fortnightly, with marked improvement and no adverse effects (EASI 9.5, cDLQI 3).

Six months later she had a marked flare due to a skin infection. Methotrexate 0.4 mg/kg/week was added with limited additional benefit (EASI 12.5, cDLQI 8). She was switched to abrocitinib 200 mg daily, with some improvement but several herpes simplex virus-driven exacerbations including eczema herpeticum (EASI 21.40). She was switched back to dupilumab 300 mg every 2 weeks.

Her AD continued to flare and she developed challenging conjunctivitis, so dupilumab was reduced to 200 mg every 2 weeks. With an EASI of 34, abrocitinib 200 mg daily was added. Within a month there was significant improvement and the conjunctivitis resolved (EASI 9.9, cDLQI 6 at 8 weeks). She remained well controlled 12 months into combined treatment, with no further herpetic exacerbations on antiviral suppressive therapy.

summary.text: A 15-year-old female with severe childhood-onset atopic dermatitis had exhausted phototherapy and conventional systemic therapy (azathioprine, cyclosporine, methotrexate, mycophenalate mofetil, oral prednisolone). Pre-biologic EASI was 25, POEM 28 and cDLQI 8. She was commenced on dupilumab 200 mg every 2 weeks, switching from cyclosporine, with some but insufficient improvement (POEM 12, cDLQI 6, EASI 11.4).

Subcutaneous methotrexate 0.3 mg/kg/week was added and increased to 0.35 mg/kg/week. She was admitted with erythrodermic AD and dupilumab was increased to 300 mg every 2 weeks. She developed conjunctivitis but had adequate control for several months. After further flares, dupilumab was switched to abrocitinib 200 mg daily with methotrexate maintained, with improved symptoms and no adverse effects.

Increasing nausea led to methotrexate being stopped. On abrocitinib alone her EASI was 27.4, POEM 19 and cDLQI 6, so dupilumab was added alongside abrocitinib 200 mg daily. She has been well controlled since 2021, remains well controlled at follow-up and stable without major adverse effects, with latest EASI 7.7 and cDLQI 6.

summary.text: A 13-year-old male with severe childhood-onset atopic dermatitis and comorbid alopecia aerata had been tried on cyclosporine and methotrexate with no improvement. His pre-biologic EASI was 26.2, POEM 16 and cDLQI 22. He entered a baricitinib trial (2 mg daily for 16 weeks, then 4 mg daily), which benefited his AA but not his AD (EASI 23.3).

After 28 weeks on baricitinib he was switched to dupilumab 200 mg every 2 weeks, with oral methotrexate 0.25 mg/kg per week added for limited response (EASI 12.8, cDLQI 9). On this combination he had worsening conjunctivitis, nausea and worsening AA, so he was switched to abrocitinib 200 mg daily. There was disease improvement with significant nausea, bloating and weight loss, and the dose was reduced to 100 mg daily.

Dupilumab was refused because of needle phobia, and on the lower abrocitinib dose he had worsening AA, inadequately controlled AD, anxiety and depression (EASI 19.8, POEM 16, cDLQI 20). Abrocitinib was increased back to 200 mg daily and dupilumab 200 mg every 2 weeks was introduced with child life specialist support. The combination benefited him significantly, with well-controlled AD over the last year and marked improvement in AA, confidence and quality of life.
